title: Brand name with a dropped vowel — zero-shot phonetic win over exact
why_real: Lyft is a dictionary word with a vowel swapped out on purpose; the user has only ever entered it as a standing dictionary fact, and the very first utterance that produces the plain word 'lift' has to be caught by sound, not by a previously-seen surface.

inputs.asr: book a lift to the airport
inputs.formatted: Book a lift to the airport.

expected.memory_aware: Book a Lyft to the airport.
expected.reason: Phonetic retrieval bridges the dropped-vowel spelling zero-shot; exact has no stored form for 'lift' and abstains no_memory.
